# std.literal

The traits a literal is sugar for: `[a, b]` and `[f(x) for x in s]` build through the `@literal("[]")` trait, and `var a: [D]T = x` fills through `@literal("[;]")` (R01.8.8). Core re-exports both, so a program's own type gets the literals by implementing them.

Import: `use std.literal.{...}`.

## `trait ListLiteral<T>`

What `[a, b]` builds when its type is `Self`: `with_room(2)`, then a `push` of each (R01.8.8).

## `trait Filled<T>`

What `var a: [D]T = x` builds when its type is `Self`: every cell `x` (R01.8.8).
